JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.3,00,00,000/- for the death of Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy in a road traffic accident dated 01.04.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the Petitioners case are as follows:
That on 01.04.2021 at about 11.45am on NH-50 Main Road, Hosapete - Bangalore Road, near Harovanahalli Village, Hosapete Tq. Bellari Dist., Mr.Kodanda Ramaswamy was on duty and traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MM-6444 along with one Jitendra Panwar and the said vehicle was driven by one Sri.Anwar Hussain and the same was proceeding from Alamatti towards Bengaluru, at that time a Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 which was driven by its driver Mr.Girish and came from opposite direction i.e., from Hidigi side towards Hospete side in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed dashed against the center road divider and dashed against the Car bearing Reg.NoKA-01-MM-6444 caused the a c c i d e n t . Immediately, after the accident Mr.Kodandaramaswamy shifted to Govt.
Hosptial, Hosapete, the doctor examined him and opined that he was brought dead.
Post Mortem conducted at Govt. Gen. Hospital, Hosapete.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, as on the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, working as Deputy Director at Executive Engineer, Cauvery Division, CWC, Jal Soudha,
Ground Floor, HMT Post Office near PMD, Bengaluru and earning salary of Rs.1,80,000/- per month and contributing entire amount to the welfare of the family.
The deceased was the only earning person, therefore, the petitioners are facing financial difficulties.
Due to the sudden demise of the deceased, the petitioners are facing difficulties.
The accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver (Respondent No.2) of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209.
The Mariyammanahalli Police have registered a case against the driver of the Toyota Innova Car in Cr.No.0047/2021 for the offences punishable u/Secs. 279, 337, 338 & 304(A) of IPC.
The petitioners are the wife and sons of the deceased.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, this petition.
4. During the trial, the Respondent No.1 died and later his Lr R.1(a) was brought on record.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent 1(a) did not appear.
Hence, placed ex-parte.
In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
5. The gist of the objection filed by the Respondent No.2/Insurance Company is as under:
This respondent denies all the averments of the petition, except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 in favour of the 1 st respondent.
It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The driver of the innova Car without wearing seat belt and without valid and effective DL drove the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further stated that the deceased also not wearing the seat belt.
It has denied the alleged accident took place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209.
There is non-compliance of Section 134(c) & 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further, the respondent No.3 denied the accident, age, income and occupation of the deceased as alleged in the petition.
The respondent No.2 has contended that compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
6. By oversight, issues for injury case is framed.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has re-framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the Lrs of the deceased Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy was died on 01.04.2021, due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver Boby Anjali vs Mahadeve Gowda on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112364033/
3 of Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-04-M-3209 as stated in the petition?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
4. What Order or Award?

11. The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the diver of the offending Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-04-M-3209, have examined the petitioner No.2 as PW.1 and got marked 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.

The Car driver of the deceased gave complaint to the police.

Therefore, the Respondent No.3 could not rebut the presumption raised in favour of the cahrge sheet averments.
The respondent No.3 has argued that the case of the petitioners is not probable since there is no damages to the front wheel and wheel suspension of the offending vehicle and has sought for taking contributory negligence of the Government Innova Car.
Only because there is no damage to the front wheel or wheel suspension, it cannot be inferred that the negligence was of the Government Innova Car.

Hospital.

Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of the deceased.

Provident Fund, Pension, Insurance and similarly any cash, Bank balance, shares, Fixed Deposits,
etc., are all a "Pecuniary advantage" receivable by the heirs on account of one's death but all these have no correlation with the amount receivable under a statue occasioned only on account of accidental death.
Such an amount will not come within the periphery of the Motor Vehicles Act to be termed as "Pecuniary advantage" liable for deduction.
2. CDJ 2023 APHC 125 : Temburu Dhana Lakshmi & Anr. Vs. Jaya Prakash & Ors.

i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:-

As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has a wife-petitioner No.1, aged about 45 years and two major sons - Petitioner Nos.2 & 3, aged about 24 & 17 years respectively.
PW.1 in his cross -examination admitted that he has completed Engineering and discontinued his M.Tech.
Petitioner No.3 is in third Semester of Engineering.
This shows that PW.1 would get job in future.
But, looking to the age of the petitioner No.3, he was a minor at the time of accident and still studying in Engineering.
Therefore, the petitioner Nos.1 & 3 wife and minor son are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

19. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged about above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was comes under 50 to 60 years age slab.
Therefore 10% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.

So Rs.11,537/- (Rs.1,15,377/-
X 10% = Rs.11,537/-) should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.1,15,377/- then it comes to Rs.1,26,914/- per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if there are Two dependents then 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.84,610/-.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,11,68,520/- (Rs.84,610/- X 11 x 12 = Rs.1,11,68,520/-).

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 45 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the sons of the deceased, they have lost their loving, care taking father.
Therefore, they are also entitled Rs.44,000/- each, in total Rs.1,32,000/- is entitled under the head of loss of consortium.

iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:-
Petitioners have stated that they have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.

Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.

iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above
, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.1,26,930/- per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,13,40,520/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,13,41,000/-.
LIABILITY 22.
The Respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore, Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Though the Petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.3,25,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,13,41,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.1,13,41,000/- (Rupees One Crore Thirteen Lakhs and Forty One Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (except on future prospects) from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount from the Respondents.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However,
the Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount, Rs.44,000/-
shall be paid to the petitioner No.2 and Rs.10,00,000/- shall be released to the Petitioner No.3 and in the remainig compensation amount 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner No.1 in any Bank for a period of 3 years and the balance amount shall be released in the name of Petitoner No.1 by way of e-Payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer on line, revised, corrected and then pronounced in the open court this the 7th day of November 2024)
(PRAKRITI KALAYANPUR) XXIII ASCJ & ACMM, Bangalore.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.3,00,00,000/- for the death of Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy in a road traffic accident dated 01.04.2021.
2.
The accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver (Respondent No.2) of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209.
The petitioners are the wife and sons of the deceased.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent 1(a) did not appear.
Hence, placed ex-parte.
The driver of the innova Car without wearing seat belt and without valid and effective DL drove the vehicle as on the date of accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has re-framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the Lrs of the deceased Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy was died on 01.04.2021, due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver Boby Anjali vs Mahadeve Gowda on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112364033/
3 of Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-04-M-3209 as stated in the petition?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
4. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The counsel for the petitioners has furnished the following decision:
MFA 8490/2010: Kumari Fazeelath Vs. Mr.Zubair Ahmed and Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that in the absence of any material to discredit what the chargesheet says, there is a presumption of correctness of the version of the police u/Sec.114 r/w Sec.32 of Indian Evidence Act., 1872 since the investigation is undertaken and regulated by the law.
Therefore, the Respondent No.3 could not rebut the presumption raised in favour of the cahrge sheet averments.
The respondent No.3 has argued that the case of the petitioners is not probable since there is no damages to the front wheel and wheel suspension of the offending vehicle and has sought for taking contributory negligence of the Government Innova Car.
Only because there is no damage to the front wheel or wheel suspension, it cannot be inferred that the negligence was of the Government Innova Car.
Moreover, the deceased was only a inmate in the car and not the driver to attribute negligence on him.
The counsel for the petitioners has furnished the following decision:
2020 ACJ 1145 : New India Assurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Sushama Mahendra Sonawane and Ors.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay has held that burden lies on the insurance company to prove that the Car driver was responsible for the accident or there was any contributory negligence on his part.
Therefore, in the absence any proof of negligence on the part of the Government Innova Car, the contentions of the Respondent No.3 cannot be accepted.
14.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of the deceased.
The counsel for the respondent No.3 has contended that the petitioner No.1 is receiving family pension of more than Rs.1,00,000/- and the same needs to be deducted from the Net Income of the deceased.
Therefore, the settled principle of law at present is that the family pension received by the wife cannot be deducted.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with Exs.P.1 to 8, this court is of the opinion that the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 driven it in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and caused the accident, as a result of which deceased L.Kodandaramaswamy has sustained injuries and shifted him to the Govt. Hospital.
Such an amount will not come within the periphery of the Motor Vehicles Act to be termed as "Pecuniary advantage" liable for deduction.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Andhrapradesh has held that the family pension cannot be termed as pecuniary advantage and is not liable for deduction.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that Family Pension cannot be deducted while computing compensation as his legal heirs are entitled to receive the amount irrespective of his accidental death.
4. 2008 ACJ 1107 : Lal Dei and Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that Family Pension cannot be deducted while computing compensation as his legal heirs are entitled to receive the amount irrespective of his accidental death.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 55 years.
Therefore, his age is considered as 55 years.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:-
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 11.
In the instant case, the deceased has a wife-petitioner No.1, aged about 45 years and two major sons - Petitioner Nos.2 & 3, aged about 24 & 17 years respectively.
But, looking to the age of the petitioner No.3, he was a minor at the time of accident and still studying in Engineering.
This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.
iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above
, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.1,26,930/- per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,13,40,520/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,13,41,000/-.
LIABILITY 22.
The Respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore, Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Though the Petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.3,25,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,13,41,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
